conviction_note: NextNav trades on the FCC Lower-900 MHz NPRM, not on a ~$1m revenue quarter. The FCC's 19 Nov agenda (released 29 Oct) leaves the item off, and the December agenda comes out after the window, so the call cannot point to a dated vote unless management says OIRA review has ended, and nothing found suggests that. A 13.5%-of-shares short (6.2 days to cover) going into a -28% month at the 52-week low gives a squeeze mechanism on any neutral-to-positive comment. The findings net to about zero. p_up 52 on an 11% abs move gives +0.44. The two numbers agree in being near zero.
bar: Consensus Q3 2026 EPS -$0.12 on revenue of about $0.99m (finviz/Zacks preview 2026-11-03, https://finviz.com/news/414498/nextnav-heads-into-q3-with-cash-partners-and-a-stalled-fcc-rule; MarketBeat earnings page also shows -$0.12 / $0.99m, https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-11-5-nextnav-inc-stock/). Two agreeing sources. The company gives no revenue or margin guidance. The stock's real bar is regulatory: the market wants any sign of the NPRM leaving OIRA review or of an FCC vote date.
positioning_check: Short interest 22.86M shares, 6.2 days to cover, as of the 2026-10-15 settlement (massive.com quote page read 2026-11-10, https://massive.com/quote/nn). That is about 13.5% of 168.8M shares outstanding and roughly 15% of float, up from 15.2M / 5.9 days in Aug 2026 (https://equibles.com/stocks/NN). The baseline's skew is null: the 25-delta value of -47.67 vol points was rejected as implausible, and the ATM spread is 48% of mid, so the option market gives no usable directional statement. Put/call OI ratio 0.31 (call-heavy). Implied event move 12.74% (indicative). Tape: -16.95% over 5 days, -27.67% over 20 days, 1.9% above the 52-week low, -65% from the high. A moderately crowded short with a capitulation run-in.

findings.finding: The FCC's tentative agenda for the 19 Nov 2026 open meeting (released 29 Oct) has six items (prison jamming, advanced air mobility in 450/24 GHz/849-851 MHz, numbering security, A-CAM I, TRS, NGSO ESIM) and no Lower 900 MHz / NextNav PNT NPRM. That follows the item being left off the 29 Oct agenda, when NN fell ~12% on 8 Oct. The next chance is the December meeting, whose agenda comes out about three weeks ahead, i.e. after this window. So the Q3 call cannot announce a scheduled FCC vote.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The October agenda omission was a -12/-13% day on 2026-10-08 (https://www.gate.com/en-us/news/detail/fcc-october-29-agenda-mixed-for-asts-spcx-nextnav-gps-catalyst-delayed-17895785), retraced +11.7% intraday the next day. The stock fell 11.1% on 2026-11-02, the first sessions after the November agenda (cause not stated in the source, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-nextnav-nasdaq-nn-stock-price-down-111-whats-next-2026-11-02/).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock fell from ~$9.6 to $8.18 after the agenda and sits at its 52-week low. What may not be priced is that the call has no dated catalyst to offer. If the market still expected the call to name a vote, the stock would not be at the low and calls would not carry the OI. The residual risk is that management's tone confirms a longer slip, e.g. into 2027.
findings.independence: The 2026-11-03 preview says management calls timing 'out of its control' and that the market has 'given up on the near-term catalyst' (https://finviz.com/news/414498/nextnav-heads-into-q3-with-cash-partners-and-a-stalled-fcc-rule). Different source, same direction.

findings.finding: The draft NPRM has been at OMB/OIRA for interagency review (DOT, Commerce, War) since March 2026. At Lytham on 2026-09-29 the CFO said 'when, not if' and gave no target date. No report found of OIRA concluding review. The call's FCC commentary is the only forward-looking content the company gives, so this release turns on whether management reports any change in OIRA status.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Regulatory-tone days on this name run ±10-13% (8-9 Oct 2026). The baseline's prior prints alternate: +7.85 (Aug 2026), -3.11 (May), +8.36 (Mar), -6.15, -10.4, -5.81, +9.06. Median |move| 7.85%.
findings.why_not_priced: The status quo, 'still in review, no date', is priced, and the stock is at its low. The asymmetric tail is unpriced: a statement that OIRA review has ended, or a vote date, would be a large upside surprise against a call-heavy, crowded-short book. No evidence of that was found, so the central size is slightly negative (a repeat of no date) with a wide upside band.
findings.independence: Communications Daily, 2026-10-05: the NPRM has been at OIRA since March and opponents are asking the White House to keep NextNav out (https://communicationsdaily.com/article/2026/10/05/nextnav-opponents-ask-white-house-to-keep-company-out-of-expected-nprm-2610020066?BC=bc_6ac02dd93082a).

findings.finding: Opposition to the NextNav plan keeps building. Since the last print, opponents petitioned the White House/OIRA directly (Comm Daily, 2026-10-05). A newly formed 'SpecTech Alliance' of 100+ companies and groups urged the FCC to reject it (TipRanks, 2026-10-12). A House Appropriations rider barring FCC funds to finalize high-power terrestrial use of 902-928 MHz passed committee on 2026-04-21.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-10-12 TipRanks piece ties a 'sharp retreat' to this resistance. The stock is -49% YTD.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: every piece is public and the stock has halved since the Q2 print. The only remaining exposure is whether management concedes changes to the band plan or a test requirement (NTIA's 2024 ask) on the call. Shrunk for the crowded short.
findings.independence: TipRanks auto-news, 2026-10-12 (https://www.tipranks.com/news/catalyst/regulatory-backlash-sends-nextnav-stock-into-sharp-retreat). Broadband Breakfast, 2026-04-22, House rider (https://broadbandbreakfast.com/house-appropriators-move-to-block-nextnav-proposal/). Three different sources, one theme, counted once here.

findings.finding: SpaceX filed (around 2026-10-26/27) asking the FCC to add NextNav's 902-928 MHz band to the draft satellite-to-mobile NPRM. On 2026-10-29 the FCC adopted the D2D NPRM without acting on that request. Management can cite SpaceX as an ally on the call, but the FCC did not take it up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A Stocktwits/TradingView item reports NN +12% on a Monday after SpaceX backed 900 MHz. The gain was given back by early November.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced as a headline and already round-tripped. It is small upside only if management reports SpaceX engagement beyond the filing (commercial talks). No evidence of that was found.

findings.finding: The balance sheet is clean going into Q3: ~$298m liquidity at 30 Jun 2026 ($228.8m cash and securities plus $69.3m of warrant proceeds collected 1 Jul). The $190m convertible was converted to ~15.2m shares, all derivative liabilities were eliminated, and ~14.8m public warrants were exercised. Q3 GAAP should therefore not carry Q2's ~$32m derivative charge (Q2 EPS -$0.24 against -$0.16 consensus), and no financing is needed. It lands as a narrower GAAP loss near the -$0.12 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print with this liquidity news (2026-08-11) moved +7.85% despite the EPS miss on derivative charges.
findings.why_not_priced: The liquidity is known. What the market may underweight at a $1.4bn cap near the low is that there is no dilution or financing overhang through 2027 at ~$15-20m quarterly burn (inferred from the -$0.12 consensus on ~169m shares, not a company number). The money buys runway while the regulatory wait goes on, not a demand ramp, so the sign is a small positive and not more.
findings.independence: The 2026-11-03 preview says debt-free with liquidity about $300m (https://finviz.com/news/414498/nextnav-heads-into-q3-with-cash-partners-and-a-stalled-fcc-rule). It rests on the same company release.

findings.finding: Positioning: 22.86M shares short (≈13.5% of 168.8M shares outstanding, ~15% of float), 6.2 days to cover at the 2026-10-15 settlement, up from 15.2M in August. The stock has since fallen 28% over 20 days and 17% over 5 days to 1.9% above its 52-week low, and put/call OI is 0.31. A non-negative regulatory comment on the call meets a crowded short and a call-heavy book.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has twice retraced a 12-13% regulatory drop within a day (8-9 Oct 2026). The last two amc prints rose +7.85 and +8.36.
findings.why_not_priced: The short build and the drawdown are visible. What is not priced is the asymmetry: with the near-term catalyst 'given up on', the release only has to avoid a new negative for shorts to cover. If the squeeze were priced, the stock would not be sitting at the low into the print with call OI three times put OI.
findings.independence: Equibles, August 2026 short interest 15.2M / 5.9 days (https://equibles.com/stocks/NN), shows the build. Baseline tape (sealed) shows the run-in.

findings.finding: Revenue bar of about $0.99m (+11.6% y/y) against $1.15m booked in Q2 (which beat the $0.92m estimate). TTM revenue is $3.98m, down 36% y/y. At a P/S near 380, revenue is not the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 revenue beat came with +7.85%, but that print also carried the liquidity news. There is no evidence the revenue line drives the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial: $0.2m either way against a $1.4bn cap.
findings.independence: The MarketBeat earnings page carries the same $0.99m (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-11-5-nextnav-inc-stock/).

findings.finding: Insiders sold 87,667 shares ($1.33m) in the 90 days to early November, all under 10b5-1 plans, including the CEO's 69,853 shares at $15.30 on 2026-09-03. No open-market insider buying was found at these lower prices.
findings.why_not_priced: Planned, tax-related sales at higher prices. Near zero information.

outside_window.finding: The December 2026 FCC open-meeting tentative agenda (released about three weeks before the meeting, likely late November) is the next point at which a Lower-900 MHz NPRM vote could be scheduled.
CFO Tim Gray presents at J.P. Morgan (Nov 12, Miami), Seaport (Nov 16), ROTH (Nov 18) and Needham (Nov 20). Any further FCC commentary there lands after the 2026-11-11 exit.
FCC November 19 open meeting itself, which does not include the NextNav item.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew (rejected) and the run-up is sharply negative. The findings mostly agree that the regulatory disappointment is in the price, and the one asymmetric element (a crowded short at the low) cuts slightly against the run-up, so the net is near zero with a small upward lean.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): FCC-agenda finding -0.75 -> -0.5, opposition finding -0.5 -> -0.4
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is not evidence): positioning finding +1.0 -> +0.75, sized on the short interest, not on the drawdown
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the clean balance sheet buys runway, not a ramp; +0.5 -> +0.4
Rule 6 (bar): two agreeing sources for -$0.12 / $0.99m, so no cap; findings kept inside the window, and the Dec agenda and Nov 12+ conferences moved to outside_window
abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged; the sum stayed at -0.1
